papers.title: Variational Principles and Machine Learning: a Numerical Analysis and PDE perspective
papers.abstract: Variational principles have played a fundamental role in the development of modern mathematics, physics, and scientific computing. From the principles of least action in mechanics to the calculus of variations and the variational formulation of partial differential equations, they have provided a powerful framework for understanding complex problems and designing reliable numerical methods. In recent years, Machine Learning has introduced a new computational paradigm, in which highly expressive nonlinear function spaces and large-scale minimisation problems play a central role. In these notes, we explore the connection between these two frameworks. We develop a variational and numerical-analysis perspective on Machine Learning algorithms, focusing in particular on their formulation as nonlinear minimisation problems. We investigate how classical concepts such as stability, consistency, approximability, and compactness acquire new interpretations in this setting, and how the variational structure of the underlying continuous problem can govern the behaviour of neural-network approximations. This perspective provides a mathematical framework for understanding existing ML algorithms while also suggesting new approaches to their design. In particular, alternative and strongly coercive variational principles can lead to more stable, reliable, and potentially more efficient computational methods.

papers.title: BayesFlow 2: Multi-Backend Amortized Bayesian Inference in Python
papers.abstract: Modern Bayesian inference involves a mixture of computational methods for estimating, validating, and drawing conclusions from probabilistic models as part of principled workflows. An overarching motif of many Bayesian methods is that they are relatively slow, which often becomes prohibitive when fitting complex models to large data sets. Amortized Bayesian inference (ABI) offers a path to solving the computational challenges of Bayes. ABI trains neural networks on model simulations, rewarding users with rapid inference of any model-implied quantity, such as point estimates, likelihoods, or full posterior distributions. In this work, we present the Python library BayesFlow, Version 2, for general-purpose ABI. Along with direct posterior, likelihood, and ratio estimation, the software includes support for multiple popular deep learning backends, a rich collection of generative networks for sampling and density estimation, complete customization and high-level interfaces, as well as new capabilities for hyperparameter optimization, design optimization, and multilevel modeling. Using a case study on dynamical system parameter estimation, combined with comparisons to similar software, we show that our streamlined, user-friendly workflow has strong potential to support broad adoption.

papers.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks
papers.abstract: We study federated spectral estimation when a large matrix is horizontally partitioned across servers that cannot share raw data. We propose FLICKER, a target-specific gradient-based power iteration that recovers a singular direction associated with a prescribed spectral target using only matrix-vector products on local blocks. Different target directions can be recovered independently and in parallel. We establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees and provide a recursive grid-search procedure for spectral target selection. Building on FLICKER, we develop BiFLICKER for federated community detection in bipartite networks, together with a sequential projected variant for nearby or repeated singular directions. Under a sparse bipartite stochastic block model, we show that properly rescaled leading singular values from a reference server provide valid global targets, and that Sequential BiFLICKER achieves a vanishing misclustering rate and exact recovery under stronger sparsity conditions. Simulations show that BiFLICKER remains close to centralized spectral clustering and is more robust than existing federated spectral baselines when local sample sizes are small. On a LastFM user-artist network naturally partitioned by country, Sequential BiFLICKER attains an overall ARI of 0.96 against centralized clustering while revealing cross-country communities with distinct listening profiles.

papers.title: Geary-type expectation identities for Mardia's sample skewness and kurtosis
papers.abstract: Under multivariate normality, we establish exact Geary-type expectation identities for Mardia's sample skewness and kurtosis. A polar decomposition of the centered Gaussian data matrix shows that each of these statistics is independent of the sample covariance matrix. This independence allows the moments of each statistic to be expressed as ratios of expectations involving polynomial numerators and powers of the determinant of the sample covariance matrix. The identities hold in arbitrary dimension $p$. To illustrate their use, we give exact expressions for the variance of Mardia's sample skewness and the third central moment of Mardia's sample kurtosis for $p=2$ and $p=3$. As an application of the exact variance formulas, we construct a moment-matched chi-square approximation to the null distribution of Mardia's sample skewness and compare its performance with Mardia's classical and mean-corrected approximations.

papers.title: PrO Filtering via Kernel Mean Embedding Dynamics
papers.abstract: Filtering methods are routinely deployed with misspecified state-space models, where Bayesian filters can diverge and become overconfident. Predictively-oriented (PrO) filtering is a recent, hyperparameter-free alternative that was demonstrated to outperform (generalised) Bayesian filtering methods when either the dynamical model or the measurement model is structurally misspecified. This can be attributed to \emph{hedging} behaviour: when an observation conflicts with the forecast, the PrO update places mass near both. Yet existing implementations of PrO filtering rely on unimodal (Gaussian) approximations, whose ability to effectively hedge is limited. This paper develops the first nonparametric, particle-based implementation of PrO filtering. The key obstacle, that PrO filtering distributions are only implicitly defined, is overcome by constructing a path from the predictive to the PrO filtering distribution whose rate is available in closed form, enabling the use of kernel mean embedding dynamics for measure transport. The resulting algorithm requires only simulation from the dynamical model and evaluations of the likelihood, with neither importance weights nor the predictive density. Moreover, as we prove, the number of pseudo-time steps it requires does not grow with the outlyingness of the observation, in contrast to transport along the Bayesian tempering path. An empirical assessment shows substantial improvement over Gaussian variation of PrO filtering in challenging nonlinear examples where Gaussian approximation is unreasonably limited.

papers.title: Design-Conditional Prior Elicitation for Dirichlet Process Mixtures: A Unified Framework for Cluster Counts and Weight Control
papers.abstract: Dirichlet process mixtures (DPMs) model variation in effects across sites or studies and in latent traits among examinees. The concentration parameter affects both the number of clusters in the sample and the population weights, yet its hyperprior is often chosen by default. We describe a method for choosing this hyperprior when the number of units is fixed by design. We calibrate a Gamma hyperprior to the analyst's expected cluster count and uncertainty about it, then examine the implied weights. If count and weight judgments conflict, Dual-Anchor selects a compromise and reports its implications for both. Across our simulations and applications, the choice of prior could change the inferred number of clusters considerably even when individual estimates changed little. A higher cluster count under an alternative prior warrants a closer look at the upper tail, where estimates can shift even when the median remains stable. The DPprior R package implements the calibration and diagnostics.

papers.title: Bayesian Computation of Copula-based Multivariate Models with an Application to Doping Detection
papers.abstract: The Athlete Biological Passport (ABP) monitors athletes for doping by comparing their biomarker readings against personalized reference ranges. These are estimated via the Bayesian ADAPTIVE model, which analyzes biomarkers separately and ignores their dependence. Building on a recently proposed copula-based multivariate extension of ADAPTIVE, this paper focuses on its computational aspects, introducing a fully joint MCMC algorithm and comparing it with a two-step Bayesian IFM estimator. Simulations show the two procedures perform comparably under a correctly specified copula, but exhibit a genuine trade-off under misspecification: the Bayesian IFM protects marginal inference, while the joint MCMC yields better-calibrated dependence estimates and is markedly faster. The two approaches are tested on a dataset containing ABP profiles of elite athletes, provided by NADO Italia, and collected as part of the project "Enhancing the methodological framework for doping detection: from univariate to multivariate testing analysis on Athlete Biological Passport profiles". Both approaches achieve consistent classification performance, providing anti-doping organizations with two concrete inferential routes for adopting a multivariate ADAPTIVE model, along with guidance on the trade-offs between them.

papers.title: Guarded Readmission Weighting for Robust Single-Index Frechet Regression
papers.abstract: Single-index Frechet regression reduces the predictor dimension for metric-space responses such as distributions, networks or curves, but its estimators are sensitive to outliers. We propose guarded readmission weighting (GRW), a one-step computation of case weights from the predictors and the response distances, usable with any weighted estimator. GRW starts from a high-breakdown fit to a multidimensional scaling surrogate, readmits cases by an add-one metric Cook's distance, downweights remote predictors and keeps a response isolation factor in the final weights. If fewer than $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ of the $n$ cases are replaced, objects far from the uncontaminated responses receive weight zero; under elliptical predictors, weights depending on the predictors only through the index and the Mahalanobis distance keep the population weighted directions in the index subspace. In simulations, three GRW-weighted estimators keep the mean projection distance to the true direction below about 0.5 under up to 30% scattered and 20% clustered bad leverage points, whereas deletion and $\alpha$-distance covariance become much less accurate as contamination grows; $\alpha$-distance covariance is more accurate in most clean, shape-outlier and good-leverage settings. In two applications, under planted contamination, the weighted surrogate-assisted and least squares directions move less than those of methods without GRW.

papers.title: Debiased Inference via Posterior Corrections for High-Dimensional Regression
papers.abstract: There has been significant progress in Bayesian inference based on sparsity-inducing priors, such as spike-and-slab and horseshoe priors, for high-dimensional regression. The resulting posteriors, however, in general do not possess desirable frequentist properties, and the credible sets thus cannot serve as valid confidence sets even asymptotically. We introduce a novel debiasing approach that corrects the bias for the entire (possibly approximate) Bayesian posterior distribution. We establish new Bernstein-von Mises theorems that guarantee the frequentist validity of the debiased law. We demonstrate the practical performance of our proposal through Monte Carlo simulations and two empirical applications in economics.

papers.title: Robust Twoblock Simultaneous Dimension Reduction and Multivariate Regression
papers.abstract: This paper introduces robust twoblock (RTB) simultaneous dimension reduction, which is the first statistically robust method to perform simultaneous dimension reduction in two blocks of variables that allows to tune the number of components in each block individually. The paper proposes both a dense and a sparse version of the new method. Sparse RTB is the first robust estimator of this kind that allows to tune both the number of components and the degree of sparsity (i.e.\ the number of variables retained) for each block individually. RTB thereby allows to optimally extract and summarize the relevant portion of information in each block of data, also in the presence of outliers. As a corollary, the estimators can be recombined into a single estimate of regression coefficients for multivariate regression that is operable when the number of variables exceeds the number of cases in each block. An extensive simulation study illustrates that the new methods are resistant to different types of outliers, while maintaining estimation efficiency across a range of dimensionality settings. These findings both hold true for the dense and the sparse method. The methods' performance is further illustrated on two example data sets and a straightforward algorithm is presented and made accessible in an open source repository.

papers.title: coherent4cast: Coherent Survival Modelling and Forecasting for History-Dependent Recurrent and Terminal Events in R
papers.abstract: Researchers studying recurrent events and terminal outcomes need software that connects incomplete event histories to interpretable forecasts and uncertainty estimates. We present coherent4cast, an R package for fitting history-dependent recurrent and terminal event models, predicting future event burden and terminal-event risk, and assessing sensitivity to incomplete observation. Users supply event histories, covariates and observation information; the package returns fitted models, dynamic forecasts, uncertainty summaries and diagnostic measures under explicitly stated assumptions. The package integrates over event histories compatible with tied dates or observation windows and supports several frailty distributions for between-subject heterogeneity. A shared probability model generates recurrent-event counts, terminal-event probabilities and restricted mean time alive. Cross-fitted targeting provides influence-function diagnostics and asymptotic inference in supported missing-at-random and right-censoring settings. Separate sensitivity analyses provide bounds under specified recording restrictions. A baseline binary-treatment interface estimates standardized treatment contrasts under consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity and independent censoring. A C++17 computational core supports the R interface. Independent numerical checks, computational benchmarks, simulation experiments and reproducible examples document accuracy, performance and inferential limitations. Outputs retain observation assumptions, convergence information and numerical diagnostics. The package, tutorials and replication materials are publicly available, supporting transparent analysis across clinical and other event-history applications.
